name: Tasks
description:
Per-session task list. Plan multi-step work, mark progress as you go, the user sees a live TODO.

Single Task tool with action switch (add, add_many, replace_plan, update, status, start, done, remove, reorder, list, clear). Prefer add_many + tasks[]. Model and human boards use canonical ordinal ids. State lives at ~/.minimal-agent/sessions/<sid>.tasks.jsonl. Current task list is auto-injected every user turn as <ma::agent::tasks>.

tool.name: Task
tool.description:
Make and monitor the task board of this session. The user sees the board live.

Use this tool for work of 3 or more steps. Also use it when the user tells you to make a sequence of steps. First, use `add_many` with `tasks` to add all the steps. Then use `start` and `done` with the task id from the board. Do not use this tool for small work of 1 or 2 steps.

Do not use the board to record information for subsequent sessions. Memory keeps that information. Do not write the board again as text in your response. Use `canceled` for a task that you stopped, and `done` for a task that you completed. A completed parent task is `done`, not `canceled`.

The tool gives an `OK` line. After it, the tool gives the updated board or a short line. A short line occurs only for `start`, `done` and `status`, and only when full results are off.

action.description:
The operation to do:
- `add`: add one task.
- `add_many`: add a task tree.
- `replace_plan`: remove all the tasks and add a new task tree.
- `update`: change a title or a status.
- `status`: set a new status.
- `start`: set the task to `doing`. The parent also starts.
- `done`: set the task to `done`. When the last open subtask closes, the parent also becomes `done` automatically. While other subtasks stay open, the parent stays `doing`.
- `remove`: remove a task and its subtasks. Use it for a task that did not start.
- `reorder`: change the sequence of the top-level tasks.
- `list`: show the board.
- `clear`: remove all the tasks.

If the tool rejects your input, try again one time. Do not add the same tasks again one at a time.

id.description: The task id from the board or from the last Task result, for example `1` or `1a`. You must give this value for `update`, `status`, `start`, `done` and `remove`.

title.description: The task title, on one line. You must give this value for `add`. For `update`, give a title, a status or the two.

tasks.description:
The task tree for `add_many` or `replace_plan`. This is the recommended value. Each item is `{title, children?}`. The `children` value is an array of subtask titles, with a depth of 2 only. Give only one of `tasks`, `items` or `titles`. Do not give `parent` with this value.

When all the subtasks are closed, the parent becomes `done` automatically. Thus, do not use `done` on the parent. Do not change the array to a string.

title.description: The title of a top-level task.

children.description: Optional. The subtask titles of this parent. Give strings, not objects. The depth is 2 only.

titles.description: An array of task titles, with no subtasks. Give only one of `tasks`, `items` or `titles`. Use `titles` only for tasks with no subtasks, or for subtasks of one `parent`.

items.description: An alias of `tasks`, with the same shape `{title, children?}[]`. The recommended value is `tasks`. Do not give `items` with `tasks`, `titles` or `parent`.

title.description: The title of a top-level task.

children.description: Optional. The subtask titles of this parent. Give strings, not objects. The depth is 2 only.

parent.description: The parent of this task. The task becomes a subtask of that parent. Give an id in the same shape as `id`. You can use it with `add`, and with `add_many` and `titles`. Do not use it with `tasks` or `items`.

after.description: Optional, for `add` and a top-level task only. The id of a top-level task. The tool puts the new task after that task and after all its subtasks. If the tool cannot find that task, or if it is a subtask, the new task goes at the end. The default position is the end.

status.description: The new status. You must give this value for `status`. It is optional for `update`. Use `canceled` for a task that you stopped. Use `done` for a task that you completed.

reason.description: Optional. The cause that the tool records when you set the status to `canceled`.

order.description: The ids of the top-level tasks, in the new sequence. You must give this value for `reorder`. The subtasks move with their parent.

filter.description: A filter for `list`. At this time, the tool ignores it and shows all the tasks.

query.description: A substring filter for the titles in `list`. At this time, the tool ignores it.

format.description: The format of the result. The default is `text`. With `text`, the tool gives an `OK` line. It also gives the board if the result is not a short line. With `json`, the tool gives the data as JSON.

parallel.description: For `start`. The tool accepts this value and ignores it. The `start` operation does not change the status of other `doing` tasks.

force.description: For `clear`. Set to `true` to clear the board when a task is `doing`. Without it, the tool rejects `clear` in that condition. The default is `false`.
